name: Overhead Lunge Pulse
summary: A dynamic lower-body mobility exercise performed in an elongated split stance with arms held overhead to build leg endurance and stretch the hip flexors.

setup: Grasp a resistance band or strap overhead with straight arms, pulling outward to maintain continuous tension.
Step one foot back into a long split stance with feet hip-width apart and the rear heel lifted high off the ground.
steps: Lower your hips downward until your front thigh is nearly parallel to the floor and the rear knee hovers just above the ground.
Pulse smoothly up and down by about one to two inches in a slow, controlled rhythm.
Maintain active tension pulling outward on the overhead implement and keep your torso fully upright.
Complete the desired repetitions or time, then press through the front foot to stand and repeat on the opposite side.
instructions.breathing: Breathe continuously and rhythmically throughout the pulsing movement without holding your breath.

common_faults.fault: Overarching the lower back to compensate for tight hip flexors.
common_faults.correction: Tuck the tailbone slightly and brace your abs to feel the stretch in the front of the trailing hip.

common_faults.fault: Bouncing erratically using joint momentum rather than muscular control.
common_faults.correction: Slow the tempo down and restrict the movement to a controlled one- to two-inch oscillation.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the front knee to cave inward.
common_faults.correction: Press actively through the whole front foot and track the knee in line with your middle toes.

precautions: Reduce the stance length or avoid lowering too deeply if you experience pain in the rear knee or groin.
